$comment: p15-oracle-074: the appearance and toggle action families (every non-excluded id of plans/cmux-next/action-surfaces.json whose family prefix is appearance or toggle: 66 today, 65 runnable and toggleFileEditorWordWrap a gap; appearance.animations.feedback.toggle is excluded). The format is browser/_tuning.json's (p15-oracle-072): gen_actions.py (p15-oracle-071) reads it and writes one case per action and engine into the flat actions suite; a context-none case is the same on both engines. Settings facet assertions: an action that writes a non-default value waits until /settings/nonDefaultKeys contains its key; one that writes the default first makes the key non-default in its before steps, then waits until the list changed; the motion actions read the arm back (/settings/motion/enabled and speed, MotionSpeed.timeScale fast 1, normal 1.5, off 0). The oracle launch is the bench config plus ui.animations.enabled false, appearance.backgroundOpacity 1 and mcp.enabled true (driver_app.py ORACLE_CONFIG). Every key these actions write is agent-settable (SettingsSchema.agentSettableKeys), so a socket caller (SettingWriter.caller) may write it; the handlers apply the value at once and return the cmux-next.json write as tracked work (AppActionContext.writeSettings), so action.run answers after the file has it. Legacy bind/run/invoke handlers report action.done. A toggle's generated restore runs it again; app_reset puts the settings back between cases. Keys as in 072: context, entrypoint, params, before, after, expect, waitFor, invariants, untested, note, chromium, divergence, gap, gap_success.

page.note: the fixture page in the focused pane: p15-oracle-222's loopback load.html (openBrowser and cmux browser navigate refuse data: URLs, BrowserURLResolver searches them), opened with focus so the socket caller's tab is selected and focused (without it TabLifecycle.newBrowser opens it unselected behind the focused tab), then navigated to #b by the bundle's CLI (a same-document navigation), so it has two history entries. The tabs facet lists a pane's browser and page tabs only (OracleTabsFacet), so on a fresh launch per case (--batch-limit 1) the fixture is the one tab of pane 0's list: page-only checks that before any case reads $page

pane-border-toggle-reads-configured.what: The handler flips the configured border (an unset layout.paneBorder reads as subtle), not the drawn one. Under the default window style (flat-sidebar-line: separation none, no border drawn) the first Toggle Pane Borders writes layout.paneBorder none, which PaneSeparation.resolve reads as cards: panes gain the density's padding and rounded corners, and no border appears or goes.
pane-border-toggle-reads-configured.chromium: chrome/browser/ui/browser_commands.cc ToggleBookmarkBar (a toggle flips the effective pref value the person sees, components/prefs/pref_service.cc GetBoolean)
pane-border-toggle-reads-configured.case: the case checks the write; no facet reads pane metrics, so the look change was found by reading the code

pane-padding-toggle-noop-default-style.what: Under the default window style the pane padding is 0 by the style's separation (impliedPadding), so Toggle Pane Padding computes off -> on as nil, writes nothing and changes nothing: action.run answers ok and padding can never be turned on from the toggle.
pane-padding-toggle-noop-default-style.chromium: chrome/browser/ui/browser_commands.cc ToggleBookmarkBar (a toggle always changes what shows)
pane-padding-toggle-noop-default-style.case: the case runs under the Panes style, where the toggle works; the default-style no-op was found by reading the handler

design-mode-unlocalized-refusal.what: The unavailable reason and the thrown refusal are English literals, not String(localized:) (CLAUDE.md, cmux-localization): a socket or palette caller in another language gets English.
design-mode-unlocalized-refusal.chromium: chrome/app/generated_resources.grd (every user-visible string is a message id)
design-mode-unlocalized-refusal.case: errorDetails pins today's English reason, so a localized fix shows as a base/head divergence on an English launch only if the text changes

react-grab-untracked-work.what: The handler starts the library load in an unstructured Task: the registry never tracks it, action.run answers before the page has React Grab, and a failure shows only as a page notice.
react-grab-untracked-work.chromium: content/public/browser/web_contents.h ExecuteJavaScriptInIsolatedWorld (the callback reports the result to the caller)
react-grab-untracked-work.case: no facet reads the page's React Grab state, so the case stays green; a facet would make it flaky until the work is returned as an ActionEffect
